concerns.text: The idea's core predictor 'exposure' (relationship between EXPOSURE and self-evaluation, moderated by features) is never operationalized. US-1 extracts authenticity, engagement, aesthetics, and self_eval, but no FR or acceptance scenario defines how 'exposure_level' (used in US-2 scenario 1 and FR-003) is measured or derived. The central moderation term cannot be built without it.

'curated_aesthetic_score' is a new moderator not present in the source idea, which names only 'authenticity cues, engagement metrics'. Either justify it as a clarifier-surfaced implied need or drop it; as written it adds a third feature stream (extraction, VIF, interaction tests) the idea did not request.

The constitution mandates distinct data-stream integrity (predictors from content, outcome from the user's own comments). The spec's assumptions cover NLP validity and demographics but never state that predictor and outcome streams are derived from separate user actions. Add an explicit assumption/requirement to preserve this scope boundary.
